question:
(i) Explain why charging by induction is effective mainly in conductors.
(ii) Compare charging by contact and charging by induction in terms of charge transfer and loss of charge by the charging body.

options.A:
(i) Induction is most effective in insulators because their charges move freely
(ii) Both contact and induction require direct touch, so the charging body loses charge in both
options.B:
(i) Induction works because protons move in conductors
(ii) Contact transfers no charge, while induction transfers charge directly from the rod
options.C:
(i) Induction occurs only if charges are fixed in position
(ii) The charging body loses charge only in induction
options.D:
(i) Induction is effective mainly in conductors because free electrons can redistribute under external influence
(ii) In contact, direct transfer makes the charging body lose some charge; in induction, no contact occurs, so it does not lose charge
